articleTitle: Model for SINR Evaluation in 5G mm Wave Ultra-Dense Network with Location-Aware Beamforming
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Location-Aware Beamforming (LAB) is an actual and promising technology for alleviating ongoing densification of stationary gNodeB (gNB) and mobile User Equipment (UE) Millimeter-Wave (mmWave) transceivers in emerging 5G and Beyond 5G (B5G) Ultra-Dense Network (UDN) scenarios. Well known problem of omni-directional links densification is an interference increase. Employing directional links between gNB and UE, based on tuning of gNB beam width and orientation, pointing to known UE location, opens up great opportunities for network densification, taking into account huge path loss in mmWave. The contribution of current research is in formalizing the relationship between UE location accuracy and the required beam width and orientation, tuned to known UE location. Proposed approach allowed us to evaluate average Signal to Interference plus Noise Ratio (SINR) and required Half-Power Beam Width (HPBW) for the set of simultaneous directional links on the UDN system level simulation model.

articleTitle: Channel Estimation and Equalization for OTFS Systems Over High-Mobility Channels
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an algorithm for channel estimation and equalization for the OTFS system using pilot symbols inserted in the delay-Doppler domain. We obtained the bit error rate (BER) curves in standard channel models EPA, EVA, and ETU with different values of Doppler frequency ranging from 1000 to 3000 Hz, indicating the rate of change of channel parameters. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm not only provides good BER performance (for EPA channel with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{d}=1000\ \text{Hz}$</tex>, at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{BER} =10^{-2}$</tex>, the difference compared to using an ideal channel estimation is only 1.8 dB) but also reduces the computational complexity when compared to other existing methods.

articleTitle: Quadrature Formation and Element-by-Element Reception of Signals with GMSK Modulation and Controlled Inter-Symbol Interference
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper proposes an approach to improving the BER performance of receiving messages when using GMSK- modulated signals by applying quadrature coherent element-by- element reception algorithms and estimating energy losses when the value decreases <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta FT$</tex>, related to the amplification of controlled inter-symbol interference caused by the conditions of signal formation. Simulation modeling is shown that with the probability of errors BER <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=10^{-3}$</tex>, when the parameter is reduced from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta FT\ 0.3$</tex> to 0.1, the energy loss is more than 3.5 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{dB}$</tex>. This loss is caused by the presence of significant inter-symbol interference. The application of the proposed algorithm of quadrature coherent element-by-element reception can be recommended in AIS systems for the identification of ships in the world ocean. An important advantage of this algorithm is its low computational complexity, which is more than two orders of magnitude less than that of the well-known Viterbi algorithms for demodulating signals with GMSK.

articleTitle: Personalized Chemotherapy Selection for Lung Cancer Patients Using Machine Learning and Computed Tomography
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The treatment of lung cancer remains a significant challenge in modern medicine, with no universally optimal treatment regimen established to date. In this study, we focused on investigating the efficacy and suitability of Carboplatin as a chemotherapy drug for lung cancer treatment. Utilizing machine learning algorithms and analyzing computed tomography (CT) data, we aimed to determine if Carboplatin or Cisplatin emerges as the best therapeutic option. Our methodology involved collecting and preprocessing clinical data, extracting deep features from CT images, developing a machine learning algorithm for image classification, and evaluating the performance of our approach. The results of our study provide valuable insights into the effectiveness of Carboplatin as a chemotherapy drug for lung cancer, aiding physicians in making informed treatment decisions based on individual patient characteristics. This research contributes to the advancement of personalized medicine and highlights the potential of machine learning and CT imaging in optimizing lung cancer treatment outcomes.

articleTitle: Low-Pass Filter for an Electret Condenser Microphone
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This article is devoted to the design of a low-pass filter for an electret condenser microphone in an electronic stethoscope. A filter with replacement of inductors by an active circuit based on operational amplifiers with a bandwidth of 1 kHz was chosen as a low-pass filter. The bandwidth ripple of the device is 1.2 dB and the stopband attenuation is 76.87 dB. The stability of the frequency response to changes in the nominal values of the elements is analyzed, nonlinear distortions and noise characteristics are considered. The result is approved by simulation using CAD Micro-Cap 12.

articleTitle: Slotted Waveguide Antenna Array in X-Band With Low Level of Side Lobes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper presents the results of calculating the parameters, designing and experimental research of the developed model of a resonant waveguide slot array antenna array of the X-band frequency with a low level of side lobes. A technique is presented for calculating the topology of slots in the waveguide slot array antenna to achieve the required distribution over the aperture, considering the effects of the mutual coupling of slots in higher waveguide modes and external space. The modeling of a waveguide-slotted array was conducted in the software package for three-dimensional electromagnetic modeling and development of high-frequency radio-electronic and antenna devices - ANSYS HFSS. The results of measurements of the radiation pattern of the waveguide slot array antenna sample in the X-frequency range are presented.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Possible Frequency Band Plans for Joint Use of 5G Broadcast and Digital TV Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: 5G Broadcast is a new concept for broadcast or multicast delivery of media services to users. This type of systems is currently under consideration for UHF band where it can be considered as a Digital Dividend after transition from Analog to Digital Television (DTV). The paper considers possible interference issues in the cases when 5G Broadcast and DTV networks operate in adjacent radio frequency (RF) channels and in neighbor transmitter cells. GE06 DTV spectrum mask Envelope Concept is mentioned as a reference point and some scenarios for joint use of 5G Broadcast and DTV proposed in EBU reports are considered for homogenous networks with frequency re-use 3. Analysis of results show that considerable interference may occur when 5G Broadcast and DTV operate in adjacent RF channels. Thus, thorough investigation of interference issues and quite complicated frequency planning are necessary in this case. Possible solutions for these problems are use of 8 MHz 5G Broadcast channel bandwidth approved in 3GPP Release 17 and UHF band segmentation that may provide use of similar types of services (e.g., DTV or 5G Broadcast) in the adjacent RF channels. Potential future introduction of new types of services in UHF band based on new types of signals will need further investigation of interference issues and corresponding frequency band planning.

articleTitle: Waveguide-Slot Phase Shifter Controlled by P-I-N Diodes System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: A new waveguide-slot phase shifter controlled by range p-i-n diodes. Models with 16 p-i-n diodes have been studied, using by computer simulation.

articleTitle: Simulation of the Active Filter Tuning Circuit Based on Digital Delay-Locked Loop
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In this paper is described an auto tuning method of active RC filters. The method is based on a Digital Delay-Locked Loop technique to tune the time constant of the active RC filter automatically. The tuning range and the tuning accuracy are analyzed theoretically. To verify the method, analog and digital part of the tuning circuit are cosimulated together. The simulation results shows that the time-constant variation is ±28<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> and can be tuned within accuracy ±3.8<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> by 4-bit code sequence.

articleTitle: Design of Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuits Bandpass Filters on GaAs pHEMT
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper presents the results of a centimeter band bandpass filters study. Bandpass filters (BPF) of different types were considered: based on interdigital, hairpin and open-loop resonator microstrip structures, as well as on lumped elements. The investigated filters are made in the form of microwave monolithic integrated circuits (MMIC) based on the GaAs pHEMT technology. They provide filtering in four sub-bands of the 5.8 … 18.2 GHz frequency band. Comparative characteristics of the filters are also given in this article, which allows us to make a rational choice of the BPF scheme during developing.

articleTitle: Synthesis Features of Optimal Signals Based on Eigenfunctions Considering the Limitations of Signal Parameters
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In the work, studies, and analysis of the synthesis features of optimal signals based on eigenfunctions were carried out, taking into account the limitations on peak-to-average power ratio (P APR) and error rate of Faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) signal, considering the symbol rate during FTN transmission. In addition, the synthesis features of the pulses for high symbol rates were considered. As a result solutions were obtained for symbol rate up to 7/<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex> without bit-error rate (BER) performance changes. Pulses had been obtained for 2/T and 3/T with P APR limitations without BER performance changes.

articleTitle: Hardware Implementation of a Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper is devoted to the hardware implementation of a convolutional neural network for image recognition systems. The goal of the work is to implement image recognition CNN in FPGA. During the research, algorithms and computer programs for image recognition at the hardware level were developed using the model-driven design approach. The developed neural network consists of 7 layers with a prediction accuracy of 99.54%. The neural network model was optimized by reducing the number of filters in the layers and changing the kernel size, resulting in a decreased prediction accuracy to 86.96%. Logical synthesis of the generated HDL code was performed. The simulation results matched the theoretical assumptions. The obtained results have significant practical value in various scientific fields including medicine, autonomous driving, robotics, quality control, etc.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach to Studying Class E Power Amplifiers with a Complex Impedance Load
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In contrast to the known publications devoted to the design of class <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex> power amplifiers (PAs) and limited to the consideration of a particular case of a real load, this paper considers an analytic method of calculation of class E PA when operating on a complex load. The relations allowing to determine real and imaginary parts of the input impedance of the load proceeding from the transistor soft-switching condition are obtained. The adequacy of the analytic model is confirmed by simulation, which shows that the relative error in the calculation of the main characteristics of the PA does not exceed 1.5%. The obtained relations can be used to synthesize a matching circuit that ensures high efficiency of the PA when operating in the frequency band.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Analysis of the Diode Frequency Mixers Using Volterra Series: Generalized Matrix Approach in the Frequency Domain
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper discusses an approach to analyzing diode mixers using nodal equations in a generalized matrix form. This method provides a full formalization of the analysis algorithm of the mixers. In this paper an algorithm for nonlinear analysis of diode mixers using Volterra series method is presented. Authors demonstrate the efficiency of developed technique by applying it to examining the nonlinear distortion of three diode mixer circuits caused by the third harmonic. The representation of the third harmonic of diode current in the frequency domain is obtained. An equivalent diode model based on this representation is introduced taking into account its capacitive parameters for the nonlinear distortion analysis. The analytical expressions for the third harmonic voltage amplitude are obtained. The maximum and minimum values of nonlinear distortion are determined. Calculation and simulation results are presented. The error between them does not exceed 2 dB.

Author Keywords: nonlinear distortion caused by the third harmonic

articleTitle: Application of Fiber Bragg Gratings for Measuring the Crack Opening Rate
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The use of fiber Bragg gratings in the device for measuring the rate of crack opening in various materials under mechanical load is considered. The technical requirements for the structural elements including tunable wavelength semiconductor laser using the Peltier element have been established. The possibility of measuring the crack opening parameters by changing the power of the radiation reflected by the Bragg grating due to change in the resonant wavelength of the grating with time delays of less than a microsecond has been experimentally demonstrated.

articleTitle: Influence of Phase and Frequency Shift on BER Performance of SEFDM Signals with Iterative Demodulation Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Authors do research influence of phase-frequency shift on BER performance of multi-frequency spectrally efficient signals using symmetrical iterative algorithm. Work demonstrates behavior of shifted BER curves with different parameters: frequency separation and number of subcarriers used for an iterative algorithm. Critical value of phase shift when the iterative algorithm does not improve BER performance is 0.76 rad in case of 1 subcarrier used for symmetrical iterative algorithm and different values of frequency separation in signal. Critical value of phase shift for frequency separation equal to 0.8 is 0.5 rad in case of different number of iterative subcarriers. As for frequency shift, for both cases the critical value is 0.1. Tables of acceptable phase and frequency shifts for different values of signal and algorithm parameters were shown.

articleTitle: Modeling the Correction of Small-Sized Rubidium Atomic Clock by a Quantum Magnetometer Under Conditions of Geomagnetic Field Variations
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper presents the results of modeling the correction of small-sized onboard rubidium atomic clock according to the signal of a quantum magnetometer, the readings of which exactly correspond to variations in the external magnetic field installed near the onboard atomic clock and registering both the magnitude and direction of the geomagnetic field in a moving carrier. Various variants of modulation of the external magnetic field are considered and the time dependences of the Allan deviation for these variants are constructed. The correlation coefficients corresponding to variations in the frequency of atomic clock and the readings of a quantum magnetometer are calculated, and the possibility of compensating fluctuations in the frequency of atomic clock caused by a change in the orientation of the carrier in geomagnetic space is demonstrated.

articleTitle: The Cooperation Experience of Peter the Great Saint Petersburg Polytechnic University and Samarkand State University Using Remote Labs
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: At the present time cooperation between universities plays an important role, allowing them to adopt best practices and improve the educational process. In the current year, cooperation has been established between Peter the Great St. Petersburg Polytechnic University, Russian Federation and Samarkand State University, Uzbekistan. As part of this cooperation, a set of remote laboratory works in electronics based on the NI ELVIS III platform and on the real laboratory equipment was tested at Samarkand State University. The paper describes the experience of using the NI ELVIS III platform, the oscilloscope Rigol DS1054z and the spectrum analyzer Rigol DSA1020 in organizing of remote laboratory works in electronics at Samarkand State University.

articleTitle: Downlink Transmit-End Beam Refinement for mmWave Communications Under Mobility
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This article discusses a method for adjusting the radiation pattern of a base station antenna array when conducting radio communications in the millimeter wavelength range for mobile user devices. The article describes a technique for selecting a training sequence of beams that minimizes the Cramer-Rao lower bound when estimating the transmission direction. The proposed technique makes it possible to reduce the beam adjustment time for transmission by 16 times compared to the conventional protocol, which improves the quality of service for highly mobile users.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Reflective-Type Phase Shifter for 5G Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The objective of this research is to develop a reflective-type phase shifter for efficient integration into 5G communication systems. The designed reflective-type phase shifter exhibits a capacity to generate 8 distinct phases, each separated by an angle of 11.25 degrees. The evaluation of its performance reveals an RMS amplitude error is below, 1.2 dB and an RMS phase error is less than 4 degrees within the frequency range of 3.52 GHz to 3.68 GHz with a maximum insertion loss of 7.6 dB.

articleTitle: Graph Analytic Method to Design a Class E Power Amplifier Operating in Frequency Band
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper considers a graph analytic method of class E power amplifier (PA) design when operating in the frequency band. Set of values in the coordinate system [ReZ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>(ω), ImZ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>(ω)], where Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>(ω) - the load impedance, lines of equal values of the relative deviation from the nominal value of output power and normalized voltage on the transistor at the time of its turning on, obtained by changing the frequency of the amplified signal. It is shown that the expansion of the operating frequency band of the PA can be ensured either by decreasing the output power or reducing the efficiency due to the increase of voltage drop across transistor before switching. The proposed method allows solving the problem of matching circuit synthesizing at a given acceptable deterioration of the listed characteristics.

articleTitle: Quantitative Analysis of Biomolecular Films: Automated Detection and Characterization of Leaves and Spiral Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Biomolecular films, pivotal in various scientific and technological domains, harbor intricate patterns that necessitate accurate analysis. In this study, we introduce a systematic methodology for the automated detection and characterization of leaves and spiral structures within biomolecular films. The method encompasses a series of meticulously designed steps, including preprocessing via grayscale conversion, edge enhancement, denoising, and contrast adj ustment. Leveraging watershed segmentation, we adeptly isolate leaves within the films. The algorithm's capability to detect spiral cores is realized through the Hough Transform and Canny edge detection. Experimental results exhibit the method's efficacy, elucidating the process visually.

articleTitle: Decision Feedback Detection Algorithm for FTN Signals: Impact of Modulation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Numerous researches are devoted to development of computationally efficient detection algorithms for Faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) signals. In this paper, the detection algorithm with decision feedback and optimal analysis interval was studied in relation to Faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) signals with QAM and PSK. A simulation model was developed to estimate the optimal analysis interval and the energy gains provided due to its application. Based on the obtained results, we can conclude that greater gains are achieved in case of PSK. This confirms the hypothesis that the considered detection algorithm works more efficiently under conditions of stronger intersymbol interference.

articleTitle: Influence Analysis of Elements Redundancy in Switching-Based DAC Calibration
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This research is dedicated to the study of switching-based calibration algorithms and its efficiency in DNL and INL reduction in a presence of elements redundancy. The previously proposed mathematical model of considered calibration algorithms is used to introduce the elements redundancy. A primary array of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M > 2^{N}$</tex> elements is generated and sorted in the ascending order with further cutting of unused edge elements. The simulation in presence of random errors is performed, which shows the nonlinearity reduction up to 80% and 90% for DNL and INL respectively.

articleTitle: Magnetic and Magnetostrictive Properties of (Tb,Nd)Fe2 Alloys
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The characteristics of materials with high magnetostrictive properties have been studied and described. The object of study is pseudo-binary compounds RFe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (R = rare earth element) with a cubic Laves structure. The characteristics of the structure and magnetic properties of substituted (Tb, Nd)Fe2 alloys are presented, the structure is refined, the lattice parameters and phase composition are determined.

articleTitle: Fully Integrated Vector Modulator in 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS Technology for 5G Front-End Modules
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper presents the simulation results of a vector modulator that can be used in TX/RX front-end modules of the fifth generation communication systems. The vector modulator is designed in 130-nm SiGe technology and demonstrates RMS amplitude error below 0.2 dB and RMS phase error less than 1.2 degree in 24–30 GHz frequency band while provides about 5 dBm input 1-dB compression point with 0 dB maximum gain and 30 mW power consumption. The layout area of the designed fully integrated circuit is less than 0.5 sq. mm.

articleTitle: Study of Changes in the Characteristics of Massive Field Electron Emission Cathodes Made of Industrial Carbon Materials Under Ar+ Ion Bombardment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Creating an effective and reliable field electron emission cathode is an important task of vacuum electronics. Field emission from massive cathodes made of industrial graphite was considered in this work. During the experiments, traditional current-voltage characteristics were obtained for the samples, long-term tests were carried out, and cathodes were exposed to argon ions. Carbon cathodes demonstrated emission current of hundreds microamperes and were able to successfully operate at pressure up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\cdot 10^{-2}$</tex> Pa. Such experimental conditions resulted in degradation of cathodes emission properties. For each stage of study the ion flux and electric field enhancement factors were calculated and analyzed. The best emission properties were shown by the sample with the lowest ash content and the largest grain size - GMZ graphite.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Strontium — 90 Vacuum Beta-Voltaic Batteries During SNF Processing by Ion Sputtering – Thermal Separation Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper is devoted to the extraction of the beta-emitting strontium-90 from spent nuclear fuel (SNF) by the ion sputtering-thermal separation (IS-TS) technology. The IS-TS technology is developed by us for the SNF processing and the selective separation of fission products. Due to theoretical considerations, it can be shown that this technology may be used to extract various useful isotopes from SNF. In particular, strontium - 90, (well-known beta emitter) can be explored via one-step IS-TS process and used to develop new beta-voltaic energy sources. The main idea of IS-TS process is the ion and thermal atomic sputtering of the SNF pellets in the inert gas plasma and these atoms differential condensation with respect to their saturated vapor temperatures downstream of some diffusion tube with inert gas flow. The selective deposition of the required chemical elements (e.g., strontium-90) is carried out in the metallic form on the internal surface of individual removable tubing sections inserted into the diffusion separation tube. Extracted strontium - 90 from prescribed tubing section is used for the fabrication of beta-active layer inside of “nano-micro-sandwich” for the manufacturing of “eternal” energy sources-a new vacuum-beta-cell (VBC).

articleTitle: Measurement Resolution of Fiber-Optic Fabry — Perot Interferometers with Different Mirrors Reflectivity
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The measurement resolution of displacement sensors based on the extrinsic Fabry–Perot interferometers with different mirrors reflectivity was experimentally studied. Spectral interferometry interrogation approach was used. The results showed that the choice of interferometer mirrors to obtain a better resolution depends on the EFPI baseline.

articleTitle: Photoluminescence of Carbon Dots Obtained by Hydrothermal Treatment of Polysaccharide Solutions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Carbon dots (C-dots) with violet photoluminescence (PL) were synthesized by ecologically clean one-pot hydrothermal treatment of aqueous solutions of natural polysaccharides. N-, S, and N/S-doped C-dots were obtained from cationic polysaccharide chitosan, anionic polysaccharide fucoidan, and their 50/50 complexes, respectively. As compared with the surface ς-potential of initial polysaccharides, the ς-potentials of their C-dots dispersions were lower due to the negatively charged -COO- groups originating from hydrolysis of polysaccharides during the hydrothermal treatment. All C-dots exhibited qualitatively similar UV/VIS absorption, PL excitation, and PL emission spectra. The influence of dopants on the spectral shifts was small (the PL emission spectra slightly shifted red from N- to N/S-, and, finally, to S-C-dots). The highest PL emission was observed for N-C-dots. Large Stokes shifts between the UV sp3-absorption and the violet PL of the C-dots are beneficial for the C-dots application in fluorescence imaging.

articleTitle: Techniques for Constructing Amplitude Frequency Characteristics of Switched-Capacitor Filters by Comparative Simulating their Circuits in Micro-Cap Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: To solve the problem of constructing the amplitude response of the switched-capacitor filters, which belong to the class of electronic circuits with a periodically changing structure, the techniques for their simulation in the Micro-Cap environment are suggested. They make possible to evaluate the nature of the change in the shape of the amplitude frequency characteristic of such filters in the time domain. As an example, a comparative analysis of the amplitude frequency characteristic of an analog second-order bandpass filter, as well as two bandpass filter circuits with switched resistors and capacitors, is given.

articleTitle: Study on Display Quality and Visual Fatigue of OLED and QD-LCD
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In recent years, as the high-resolution (HD) display technology continues to develop, the widespread utilization of display technology has become a reality, while the incidence rate of visual fatigue surged as well. Organic light-emitting diode (OLED) and quantum dot liquid crystal display (QD-LCD) are two display technologies with respective advantages. In order to study the display quality of the two display technologies and their impact on visual fatigue, we applied a combination of subjective and objective evaluations. The experiment consists of 41 volunteers, and their subjective feedbacks are adopted to compare the display quality and the impact on visual fatigue of two display technologies under various viewing tasks. Results show that teenage subjects and myopic patients suffer from greater eye fatigue after watching quantum dot liquid crystal displays (QD-LCD) TV as opposed to watching organic light-emitting diode (OLED) TV, and there is no significant difference between the two display technologies in other occasions.

articleTitle: Open-Source and Non-Commercial Software for Digital ASIC Design
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This article devoted to open-source and non-commercial software for the physical design of digital integrated circuits, realizing a flow for the main stages of physical implementation. Open-source and non-commercial software for digital integrated circuits design has been compared with similar commercial software in terms of functions performed.

articleTitle: Efficiency of Coherent Processing Algorithms for FTN Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper presents a comparison of different algorithms for processing FTN signals using different shaping pulses in cases of different deviations (time, frequency, time). A simulation model of information transmission using FTN signals has been developed for the coherent element-by-element algorithm, decision feedback and MLSE algorithm. The BER performance was obtained and the computational complexity of the algorithms was evaluated, as well as the efficiency of the algorithms at different deviation. Boundaries of possible deviation at which processing is still possible were determined.

articleTitle: A 1 km Line-of-Sight Ultraviolet Communication System with a Data Rate of 26.6kbps
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Ultraviolet communication (UVC) has emerged as a promising solution for close-range communication within the intricate electromagnetic setting. The atmosphere's attenuation, however, restricts the scope and rate of communication. We demonstrated a line-of-sight (LOS) UV communication system. In our system, we employed ultraviolet light-emitting diodes (LEDs) in our system to transmit the signal light with a broad radiation angle and use lenses to enhance the communication range. We propose a combined approach of theory and practice to analyze the feasibility of a LOS UVC system.

articleTitle: System Level Simulation of MEMS Pressure Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The article deals with designing the system model of MEMS pressure sensor for the chosen technical requirements. MEMS pressure sensor consists of a micromechanical capacitive sensitive element and a programmable application specific integrated circuit. The synthesis technique of the pressure sensor system model has been developed. The method is based on an analytical parameter estimation and preliminary schematic simulation and suitable for top-down design methodology. The obtained results allowed to select the pressure sensor design and to develop the technical requirements for pressure sensor components: a sensing element and an integrated circuit. System level simulation of MEMS pressure sensor was made and SINAD performance of 67.8 dB was obtained.

articleTitle: Application of Root-MUSIC Algorithm for Enhancing Spatial Resolution of Optical Coherence Tomography Images of Optical Fibers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Properties of optical fibers are strongly related to their geometric dimensions and the properties of the materials they are made of. Therefore, for precise inspection and prediction of optical fibers properties it is desirable to perform non-destructive measurement of their internal structure. Optical concrete tomography is one of the commonly used imaging technologies that produces two- and three-dimensional images of transparent objects with high spatial resolution. However, with traditional signal processing techniques, axial spatial resolution is inversely proportional to the spectral width over which the measurement is made. Improvement in resolution by simply increasing the bandwidth is limited due to the practical properties of available optical sources and the influence of material dispersion. In this paper, we propose to apply the root-MUSIC method to optical coherence tomography interference signal processing and demonstrate that, under certain conditions, several-fold improvement in axial spatial resolution can be achieved. Experimental verification of the effectiveness of the proposed approach was carried out by measuring the geometric parameters of cross-sections of multimode and single-mode optical fibers.

articleTitle: MEMS Low-Magnetic Electric Heating Chip for Temperature Control of Alkali Vapor Cell
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The article is devoted to solving the problem of ensuring accurate control of the operating temperature of alkali vapor cells for quantum frequency standards and magnetometers in order to increase the stability of their parameters. For this purpose, a low-magnetic electric heating chip, containing a temperature control system, which consists of a thin-film heater and a temperature sensor, has been developed and manufactured by MEMS technology. The system has such a design that the magnetic fluxes generated by the electric currents passing through its individual elements mutually extinguish each other. The heating chip and the cesium vapor MEMS cell were integrated into the physical package of the atomic clock. The magnitude of the magnetic field induced in the center of the MEMS cell was estimated by measuring of the atomic clock resonant frequency shift at different heater currents. It was found that the dependence of the parasitic magnetic flux density on the heater current has a linear character with a coefficient of 2.1 nT/mA.

articleTitle: Measuring the Statistical Characteristics of a Microwave Fiber Optic Link in 0.5-12.5 GHz Range
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: A techniques to measurement noise figure of microwave fiber optic transmission line is given. Two method of noise figure measurement - the Y-factor method and the direct noise figure measurement method - are discussed and compared. The structure of lab setup of microwave fiber optic line and characteristics of its component, and characteristics of used measurement equipment are given. We measure output noise power spectral density, power gain and noise figure. Lab setup line has noise figure 28.5… 32.5 dB in studied frequency range.

articleTitle: Investigation of Polarization Characteristics of Active Tapered Fibers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: A stand for studying the polarization characteristics of optical fibers by the Jones method was created and the characteristics of two samples of active tapered sT -DCF fibers were studied. Jones matrix and birefringence beat lengths for two samples was performed.

articleTitle: Optimization of Current-Driven Passive Mixer Conversion Gain Taking Into Account the Parameters of the Low Noise Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper presents a method for optimization of conversion gain of current-driven passive mixer considering parameters of the low noise amplifier. It is shown that the proper choice of the low noise amplifier load inductor and coupling capacitor allows an increasing of the mixer conversion gain in 5.34 dB comparatively with the conventional design. The low noise amplifier and the current-driven passive mixer with maximum conversion gain are designed at around 2.4 GHz range using 180 nm CMOS process. The comparative characteristics of various load inductor and coupling capacitor are considered.

articleTitle: Coercive Field Values and Shape Features of FE Loops in PMN-20PT at Low Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The classic way to describe ferroelectric (FE) loops comes down to specifying only basic parameters. Usually, it is not enough to fully describe the loop shape. In our study we proposed a simple method which provides information about asymmetry in measured FE loops or switching rate. A three-percentile method was proposed for a more detailed description of FE loops. Coercive field values and FE loop shape properties of PMN-20PT single crystal at low temperatures were determined. Analysis of FE loops shape measured at different frequencies led us to assumption of existence of several polarization switching mechanisms with different characteristic times. The model function for temperature dependence of corrective field was refined.

articleTitle: Supercomputer Simulation of Amino Acid Molecules High-Frequency Polarizability in THz Electric Field
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The study of the dynamic properties of amino acid molecules in external terahertz range electric fields was carried out using the method of supercomputer molecular dynamics simulation. Characteristic features of biomolecular responses to external electric fields were identified. Based on the conducted calculations, families of spectrograms were constructed for the molecules of glycine, tryptophan, and phenylalanine. The selection of substances, the dynamics, structural and functional properties of the domain, as well as the physical basis of its interaction with matrix elements, are discussed. The conclusion is drawn that embeddable biomolecular domains, or implants, are promising for signal transformation in heterogeneous hybrid microelectronics. Approaches to determining the structural, dynamic, and functional properties of biomolecular components are considered.

articleTitle: Swept-Source Optical Coherence Tomography System with an On-Chip K-Clock Based on Silicon Photonics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper presents the design of a photonic integrated circuit (PIC), which represents a key step towards a fully integrated swept-source optical coherence tomography (SS-OCT) system. In addition to the on-chip interferometer and reference arm, the PIC includes an optical clock implemented through a tunable unbalanced Mach-Zehnder interferometer and a balanced detection scheme. The chip is developed based on a silicon-on-insulator platform and operates in a 1300 nm wavelength range suitable for tissue and inner organ diagnostics. The simulation results in the Ansys Lumerical software show the good performance of the proposed SS-OCT device beyond the zero-delay point. The implementation of the optical part of the OCT circuit on PIC can provide a trade-off between miniaturization, cost, and system performance, which can unlock new perspectives for its application.

articleTitle: Automatic Axis-Aligned High-Speed Optical Wireless Communication System Based on Laser Diode
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The current RF wireless communication spectrum resources are facing significant scarcity, which hampers their ability to support the requirements for ultra-high data rates and ultra-low latency. Laser Diodes (LD) based optical wireless communication (OWC) has emerged as a potential alternative technology that has garnered considerable attention. OWC utilizes the abundant spectrum of light and offers several advantages, including rich bandwidth, strong security, and high trans-mission rates. In this paper, we propose an automatic axis-aligned high-speed optical wireless communication system based on laser diode. Using the camera and the 2D steering, we demonstrate a mobile real-time OWC system over a distance of 0.8 m and a field angle of ±10°. This system is based on the 10 Gigabit Ethernet protocol and can consistently deliver TCP data transmission at a rate of 9.36 Gbps.

articleTitle: Algorithm for Coherent Detection of Spectral-Efficient Signals with Decision Feedback and Extended Observation Interval
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The article provides a derivation and description of an algorithm for detection of spectral-efficient signals with controlled intersymbol interference. The presented algorithm is based on a common technique with decision feedback, however, unlike known approaches, it assumes modification by expanding the observation interval. This allows us to use estimates of signals subsequent in the sequence using a method other than direct averaging according to the maximum likelihood criterion.

articleTitle: A Technique for Improving the Accuracy of RMS Measurement for the Low-Pass Filtration Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The low-pass filtration method is one of the most popular RMS measurement methods. This method is characterized by flexibility of use and ease of finding of the final error rna the RMS measurement. The approach is suitable for measuring both polyharmonic and pure-sinusoidal impacts, which ensures its wide practical use. It is known that the main source for the appearance of a systematical error is due to the finite stopband rejection of the applied filter. This setting results in incomplete suppression of noise that occurs after squaring the input signal. This paper proposes an approach that can greatly reduce this error source. The approach is based on calculating a correction for an interference signal that is not completely suppressed by the used filter of low-pass type. The proposed technique is characterized by high efficiency for the case of an input polyharmonic-type with low harmonic coefficients or pure-sinusoidal type signal. To improve efficiency, it is recommended to perform an initial phase adjustment and an additional frequency evaluation. These tasks allow to effectively apply the cross-zero technique. Analytical formulas are proposed the use of which ensures one to calculate the final error value for the polyharmonic and case of both sinusoidal input signal impacts. The mathematical modeling was carried out in Matlab package.

articleTitle: Field Trial on DTMB-A for the Coverage Performance of HDTV Program Under High Mobility and Spectrum Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The coverage performance for Digital Television/ Terrestrial Multimedia Broadcasting-Advance system and 3GPP “Further evolved Multimedia Broadcast Multicast Service”, long-term evolution-based broadcasting system defined by release 16 (R16) with different working parameters has been evaluated through the field trial in Shenzhen with a focus on high-speed mobility car with reasonably high spectrum efficiency. The trial uses the same transmitter facility of same the RF hardware, at the same frequency and with the same power. Results show that terrain is major deterministic factor for coverage performance for each system and well-designed longer time-interleaver for R16 is indispensable to users' satisfaction under this application scenario.

Author Keywords: Further evolved Multimedia Broadcast Multicast Service (FeMBMS)

articleTitle: Picosecond Optical Pulse Generator for High-Power Infrared and Visible Fiber Lasers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper describes the implementation of a semiconductor laser short pulse source. The laser diode operates in gain switch mode. Design and testing of the source are described as well as some problems and solutions to them. The shortest pulse generate has the duration of 250 picosecond.

articleTitle: Pulse-Shaped SEFDM Signals in Frequency-Selective Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: An approach for improvement of bit-error rate (BER) performance of spectrally efficient frequency division mul-tiplexing signals (SEFDM) with high order modulation in LTE fading channels is proposed. It is based on using of optimal pulse-shaped SEFDM symbols, lattice based demodulation algorithm in conjunction with ZF equalizer based on the equivalent OFDM representation. Such modulation approach reduces the number of adjacent sub carriers, which interfere with each other in fading channel. Therefore, the demodulation algorithms, which consider adjacent sub carriers, perform better. BER performances of pulse-shaped and traditional SEFDM-signals with various values of compression coefficient are considered. The BER performance of pulse-shaped SEFDM-signals with QAM-16 modulation in LTE fading channels are improved, compared to the one of traditional SEFDM-signals.

articleTitle: Dielectric Properties of Fibrous Composite Materials Based on Piezoelectric and Conductive Polymers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In this work, a comparative experimental study of the dielectric properties of films based on the piezoelectric polymer PVDF and its copolymer PVDF-TrFE, as well as fibrous samples made from PVDF-TrFE was carried out. The dielectric properties of biocompatible polymer composite materials based on PVDF - TrFE copolymer fibers modified by coating with various conductive polymers (polypyrrole and polyaniline) were also investigated and analyzed, and the dielectric response of the synthesized composites to environments with different acidity was studied. It was found that the studied composites based on piezoelectric and conductive polymers are characterized by a strong dependence of capacitance values on the acidity of the environment. The results obtained can be considered as the basis for creating working elements of new medical sensors that respond to the acidity of the environment.

Author Keywords: response to the acidity of the environment

articleTitle: Study of Magnetic Nanoparticles with Citrate Shell in Aqueous Solution by Laser Correlation Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The behavior of magnetite nanoparticles in an aqueous ferrofluid with citrate stabilization is discussed. The laser correlation spectroscopy was used for experimental study of their agglomeration. It was carried out by the standard equipment supplemented by the possibility of applying an external magnetic field. It was shown that the material tends to form relatively large aggregates even without the field, and in the case when it is switched on they begin to grow. The increasing of their dimensions continues until some point when the resulting structure becomes unstable and the aggregates defragment. Possible physical causes of such features are considered.

articleTitle: Dimension Weight Scanning Module Based on ESP32 for Warehouse Management System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper is devoted to development of an adjustment model of a dimension-weight scanning module for warehouse management system. Its main purpose is to test and debug a warehouse management system and its modules without purchasing an expensive industrial model. The main advantage of the development of the proposed device is to reduce the module cost, while maintaining the functionality. To obtain data about a stock-keeping unit a periphery such as laser-ranging and load cell sensors are used. It is also necessary to identify items by QR or barcode, which will be carried out using the camera module and computer vision algorithms. Finally, the data is sent to the WMS server via Wi- Fi. The methods and techniques to increase system performance and extension of a dimension-weight scanning module functionality have been proposed.

articleTitle: Efficient Thin-Film Lithium Niobate Integrated Optical Modulator with Wide Waveguides Fabricated by Contact Photolithography
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: An integrated optical phase modulator based on thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) was fabricated and experimentally tested. The original topology of the modulator made it possible to use wide waveguides fabricated by contact photolithography with limited resolution. High-order mode suppression by more than 20 dB was carried out by electrodes and inherently multimode rib waveguides became quasi single-mode. The influence of the geometry of rib waveguides and the interelectrode gap on the suppression of high-order modes, as well as on the efficiency of electro-optical modulation, was analyzed. The obtained value of the VπL parameter for experimental samples was 4.0-4.3 V·cm, which is in good agreement with the results of theoretical analysis and is comparable with the data known from the literature for TFLN integrated optical modulators with a similar interelectrode gap. Photolithography compatible fabrication is very attractive for low cost mass production of TFLN photonic integrated circuits.

articleTitle: Superlattices in CsPbBr3 Nanocrystals Wavelength Dependent Impedance Spectroscopy($\lambda$-IS)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In this work a study of the exciton dynamics in perovskite CsPbBR3 nanocristales which shows, according to the XRD results, a superlattice signature observed in the literature. Wavelengths dependent Impedance spectroscopy (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex>, -IS) characterization shows different shape and size of arcs for each wavelength studied. The Nyquist plot shows an absence of internal interaction for blue wavelengths. As the carrier density increases, significant changes can be observed in the resistive, capacitive, and constant-phase element parameters, as evidenced by the fits to data and equivalent circuit. And constant phase element responsible for the dynamics of charge carriers occurs only once in the equivalent circuit for wavelengths of 605nm and twice for the rest of the wavelengths studied.

articleTitle: Simulation of a Capacitive MEMS Accelerometer Based on SOI Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The results of simulating a capacitive MEMS accelerometer based on SOI technology are investigated in this study, focusing on the stability against impact loads. The functional material for the sensing element was monocrystalline isotropic silicon with a crystallographic orientation of <100>. The following findings were discovered: a working acceleration measurement range of ±15g; mechanical sensitivity of the sensing element at 0.007 μm/g; capacitive sensitivity of the sensing element at 14 fF/g; resonance frequencies of 1632.2 Hz along the x-axis and 1522 Hz along the y-axis; total capacitance of the electrode sensing structure is 4.65 pF.

articleTitle: A Two-way Automatic Alignment Visible Light Communication System Based on Red Laser
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Visible light communication(VLC) has shown in explosive growth recent years, and LEDs based visible light wireless communication has the potential to change lives in the future with applications such as LiFi, smart lighting and indoor positioning. Due to the low bandwidth of LED devices, the VLC systems using LDs(laser diodes) as light sources can achieve faster transmission speed. In this paper, we propose a high-speed visible light communication system with automatic alignment function using red laser. Each tranceiver in the system can be moved in the angle of view of another, and be aligned in real time using cameras, computers and two-dimensional turntable. TCP data transmission rate more than 700 Mbps with a distance of 6 m free-space link, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 10^{\circ}\text{angle}$</tex> of view was achieved.

articleTitle: Influence of External Effects on the Optical Characteristics of an Optical Fiber
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The influence of such external influences as bending, axial tension and torsion on the optical and strength characteristics of the optical fiber has been studied. It is shown that the tension of the bent optical fiber causes an increase in optical losses compared to the case of the unstretched fiber. It should be taken into account that this effect affects not only the signal-to-noise ratio at the output of the system, but also the possibility of unauthorized access. The risk of shortening the service life of the fiber also increases. The combined effect of bending and torsion of the fiber also causes deterioration in the transmission characteristics of the fiber and its mechanical strength. Thus, it has been shown that during the installation and operation of an optical cable system, situations that cause bending, axial tension and torsion of the optical fiber, and even more so their combined effects, should be avoided. Reflectometric methods can be used to diagnose these effects.

articleTitle: Remote Control in the Manipulator System “Sensor Glove ― Robotic Hand”
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The development of a manipulator system with remote control of a robotic hand can be aimed at restoring the motor function of the human hand. In addition, such a system can be used to create bionic prostheses for people with disabilities. The robotic hand is controlled by a sensor glove worn on the human hand. In this work, ionic electroactive polymers are used as sensors placed in such a glove. The connection circuits for electronic components included in the sensor glove and robotic hand are presented. The commands loaded into the master and slave Arduino N ano boards, which provide wireless data transmission and reception, respectively, are given and commented on. Remote control is implemented by two NRF24L01 + radio modules, one of which operates in transmitter mode and the other in receiver mode.

articleTitle: Silver Ion Emission Using Chalcogenide Glass
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Experiments on ion emission in vacuum with a solid-state ion emitter based on GeS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-AgI at an accelerating voltage of 2.5-15 kV were carried out. The composition of particles deposited on the substrate after emission was studied, the conductivity properties of the solid electrolyte were determined: the specific ionic conductivity at 25°C 7.5.10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup>S.cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> and the activation energy at 75.10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> eV.

articleTitle: Spun Fiber Model Based on Jones Matrix Formalism
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Expressions for the Jones matrix of a real spun fiber were obtained within the framework of the polarization element model with phase anisotropy and weak deviation of fiber eigenmodes from circularly polarized states. These expressions can be used to model and calculate fiber optic circuits with spun fibers within the Jones matrix formalism. The resulting matrix expressions contain three independent parameters that are unpredictable in fibers and must be varied during the modeling process.

articleTitle: Study and Analysis of the Normal-State Nernst Coefficient in the $\mathrm{Y}_{1-\mathrm{x}}\text{Ca}_{\mathrm{x}}\text{Ba}_{2}\text{Cu}_{2.6}\text{Cu}_{2.6}\text{Co}_{0.4}\mathrm{O}_{\mathrm{y}}$ System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: We present the results on the normal-state Nernst coefficient, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex>, in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{Y}_{1-x}\text{Ca}_{x}\text{Ba}_{2}\text{Cu}_{2.6}\text{Co}_{0.4}\mathrm{O}_{y}$</tex> system. We have measured the temperature dependences of the Nernst coefficient in samples with different levels of additional calcium doping (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x=0-0.2$</tex>) and analyzed them quantitatively within a narrow-band model. The use of data on the parameters of the energy spectrum, previously obtained by the thermopower analysis for the same samples, allowed us to satisfactory describe the experimental <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q(T)$</tex> dependences and to determine the values of the charge carrier mobility and the degree of asymmetry of the dispersion law for all samples. Variation of these values with increasing calcium content is discussed taking into account the changes in other energy spectrum parameters.

articleTitle: Noise Stability Assessment of Virtual Magnetic Dipoles When Placed on a UAV
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper considers the use of virtual magnetic dipoles for direction finding of incident electromagnetic waves. Measurement of electromagnetic wave characteristics is performed based on vector antenna elements that are placed on a small UAV. To assess the stability of the proposed method to noise exposure, the noise of the voltages measured by the antenna elements was carried out. The obtained results are confirmed by bearing graphs without noise exposure and with noise felting, as well as statistical characteristics of direction finding.

articleTitle: Equivalent Number of Bits in Delta-Sigma Analog-to-Digital Converter in Automatic Control and Monitoring Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The dynamic error of delta-sigma ADC working in analog information input devices of control and monitoring systems (CMS) is investigated. The traditional structure of the analog information input unit in CMS contains a sensor of physical quantity, ADC, analog anti-alias filter, amplitude multiplexer and analog storage device. These functional units determine the static and dynamic errors of the analog-to-digital conversion process. At the same time the equivalent number of bits of delta-sigma ADC, which are widely used today in the devices of radio engineering, automation and communication, is determined by the total error of the above mentioned functional nodes, consistently converting the output signal of the sensor. It is shown that in order to reduce dynamic errors it is reasonable to leave only the sensor and delta-sigma ADC in the signal conversion chain, which in this case is introduced into the channel of each sensor. In this case, to assess the influence of the dynamic characteristics of the sensor it is proposed to approximate its signal spectrum as a function of the signal spectrum at the output of the anti-alias low-pass filter with Butterworth approximation. Analytical dependences for determining the errors of analog-to-digital conversion with delta-sigma ADC are obtained, allowing to solve direct and inverse problems of CMS input circuit design: to evaluate the chosen variant or to design CMS functional units with the required characteristics.

articleTitle: A 10 Gb/s Broadband Transimpedance Amplifier in 0.18 μm CMOS Technology for Optical Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This study presents the design of a 10 Gb/s high-speed optical receiver (RX), incorporating various techniques for bandwidth extension. The RX architecture consists of a pseudo-differential transimpedance amplifier (TIA), a continuous-time linear equalizer (CTLE), and an output buffer stage based on f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>-doubler. Additionally, inductive peaking technique is employed to further extend the bandwidth. The RX design is implemented using 0.18 μm CMOS technology, achieving a transimpedance gain of 55 dBΩ and a bandwidth of 7.5 GHz. A comparison with the conventional RGC-TIA reveals a bandwidth extension ratio (BWER) of 1.8 for the proposed design. The RX overall consumes a power of 14 mW from 1.8-V voltage supply, while maintaining an average input-referred noise current below 18.2pA/√Hz

articleTitle: Effect of Synthesis Time and Component Excess on LAGP Phase Composition
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Solid-state lithium-ion batteries with NASICON-type electrolyte are a promising direction of the current source's development. One of the main problems of lithium-conducting materials with NASICON-type structure, LAGP in particular, is their relatively low electrical conductivity since the grain boundary and low-conductivity phases decreases the average conductivity of the material. The change of chemical composition during synthesis due to volatilization of the most mobile components directly affects the properties of the material and its crystallization. However, the method to influence the components ratio in LAGP has not yet been provided. Thus, the study of the synthesis time and the attribution of DTA exothermic peaks to specific phases are urgent scientific questions.

articleTitle: New Methodology of Defect State Control in Backbone Unidirectional Fiber-Optic Communication Lines
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The necessity to study the evolution of the trunk fiber-optic communication line for information transmission in one direction under special operating conditions has been substantiated. These conditions are related to the design features of the structure of trunk pipelines in the North-West region of the Russian Federation of Gazprom transgaz St. Petersburg. A new methodology of defect detection on the backbone fiber-optic line is proposed. Measurements have been made on different sections of the main fiber-optic communication lines of Gazprom transgaz Saint-Petersburg. Fiber trace software analyzed the obtained data and developed a new program for drawing up a protocol based on the measurement results. New defects on the backbone fiber-optic communication line are determined. The degradation processes of the previously determined defects are evaluated. A comprehensive comparative analysis of the data obtained during ten years of fiber-optic line operation is performed and the evolution of its degradation is evaluated. The obtained data, unlike previously used estimates, allow to determine more correctly and reasonably the terms of scheduled repairs on the line or the expediency of its replacement with a new one (overhaul of the route), as well as to coordinate the points of new connections to the line, which is necessary to do with constant changes in the network of gas consumers and modernization of the pipeline system.

articleTitle: Study of Algorithms for Correction of Navigation Systems of Spacecraft Re-Entering the Atmosphere
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Various navigation algorithms for processing and filtering navigation information are presented, namely Kalman filtering, self-organisation method and genetic algorithm. A scalar estimation algorithm is considered, which allows the formulation of an independent mathematical equation for estimating a particular component of the state vector. To evaluate the performance of the investigated navigation algorithms, an original methodology is used, assuming the use of the inertial navigation system error equations in determining the position of the aircraft, acting as criteria for evaluating the accuracy, formulated on the basis of the model of motion of a gyrostabilised platform. Real laboratory tests are passed to verify the achievable accuracy estimation using the proposed navigation algorithms under semi-natural experimental conditions. The results of laboratory experiments with real navigation systems have demonstrated the high accuracy and robustness of information processing through self-organisation algorithm and genetic algorithm.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Strength of a Multilayer Electromagnetic Shield to the Effects of Temperature
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: An important issue in the development of technical systems is their protection from the effects of electromagnetic radiation, which can be solved using thin Ni films. In this work, samples of thin Ni films with a thickness of 27 to 145 nm were studied. An electromagnetic screen using poly-para-xylylene (thickness <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$15\ \mu\mathrm{m})$</tex> and nickel (thickness 65 nm) provides shielding of at least −22 dB over the entire researched frequency range (from 2 to 6 GHz) when exposed to temperatures up to 140°C.

articleTitle: Detection of a Point Dipole Signal by a Quantum Gradiometer Under Conditions of Geomagnetic Field Variations
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper analyzes the effect of geomagnetic variations on the results of measuring the coordinates of a moving point magnetic dipole using signals from a laboratory quantum gradiometer in the form of two M<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Z</inf>-type quantum magnetometers with an optical lamp pumping. It is shown that geomagnetic field variations within the laboratory are random and do not depend on the location coordinates of the magnetometers. In addition, the paper discusses the proposed method for determining the distance from the sensitive magnetometer sensor to the magnetic dipole.

articleTitle: Algorithm for Modeling Fringing Fields of Multipole Ion-Optical Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Integral potential representation is used to design fringing field structures of multipole fields. This approach gives analytical (but integral) form of potential in a space if potential distribution near the multipole axis is known. Equal potential surfaces of fields with different parameters and with given potential distribution specified near the axis are build. Example of trajectory construction in the fields are given.

articleTitle: Characteristics Analysis of Different Models of Quantum Frequency Standard on Mercury-199 Ions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: New trends in the development of navigation systems and the tasks to be solved using global navigation satellite systems, as well as the creation of the basis for deep space exploration have forced changes in the requirements for quantum frequency standards, especially in terms of frequency stability without communication sessions with the Earth. The corresponding new requirement quantum frequency standard is the quantum frequency standard on mercury-199 ions. This is now the most promising frequency standard for space systems, especially for deep space exploration. To determine the directions of modernization of the design of the quantum frequency standard on mercury-199 ions (by the new requirements), we collected and summarized information about the current research of the quantum frequency standard on mercury-199 ions in different countries of the world (USA, Russia, European Union, and China). For the first time, we performed an extended analysis comparing the characteristics of different models of quantum frequency standard on mercury-199 ions, which differ mainly in the ion traps and light sources for the excitation of mercury-202. The analysis of the technical characteristic of the quantum frequency standard on the mercury-199 ions, as well as our data on calculations of ion trap design with different electrode configurations, showed that long-term stability (10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> s) of the USA and Chinese models is an order of magnitude higher than that of the Russian and European Union models. The data are comparable in terms of short-term stability at the initial stage of operation. This confirmed our calculations from the parameters of the traps on the effect of electrode fabrication technologies on frequency stability. At present, this problem has not received adequate consideration in the world.

Author Keywords: quantum frequency standard on mercury-199 ions

articleTitle: Full Compensation of Doppler Effect in Satellite Geolocation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper presents the problem of the influence of the Doppler effect on the accuracy of determining the location of a radio source signals of unknown form in a satellite geolocation system (SGS). In contrast to the traditionally used Doppler frequency shift-only compensation method, a direct Doppler scaling factor compensation method is considered here. By modeling a real satellite geolocation system using the SGP model and orbital parameters in the TLE data format, the possibility of a significant increase in the accuracy of the satellite geolocation system using the considered method is shown.

articleTitle: Optical and Electrical Properties of Polymer Nanocomposite Dielectric Based on Polyvinyl Alcohol and Fullerenol C60(OH)44
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The optical and electrical properties of PVA films and PVA + C6o(OH)44 nanocomposite have been compared. It was found that even a small addition of fullerenol molecules to PVA leads to its coloration, and the nanocomposite films become opaque in the UV region of the spectrum. It is shown that at elevated temperatures, noticeable differences in the conductivity and low-frequency dielectric permittivity of PVA films and PVA+fullerenol composite films are observed. Their possible causes are analyzed.

articleTitle: Active Compensation of Higher Harmonics in a Switched-Mode RF PA
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The estimate of total harmonic distortion (THD) correction capability was given when having non-ideal phase or amplitude alignment in active compensator of higher order harmonic components. The estimate of efficiency loss due to usage of harmonic compensator in a switch mode power amplifier (PA) was given. For example, efficiency of PA decreases by 7-10% when total harmonic distortion KTHD= 20% and active compensator used. Moreover, amplitude and phase deviation in the active compensator results in less compensation capability. Achievable higher harmonics level reduction is more than 40 dB, when amplitude deviates less than 1% or phase error is no more than 2.5 deg.

articleTitle: Acousto-Optic Modulator Control System in the Cesium Quantum Frequency Standard with Optical Pumping and Detection for Ground-Based Synchronization Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Problems that arise in the operation of a quantum frequency standard (QFS) on cesium-133 atoms when using laser pumping to create a population inversion are noted. The key device in such designs is the acousto-optic modulator (AOM). For its effective operation in generating a signal with a given frequency, a control system with various feedback circuits plays an important role. This paper presents a new design of a control system for an acousto-optical modulator for a cesium frequency standard for multifunctional applications. Such design standards have very high requirements for weight, size and accuracy characteristics. The studies carried out showed the amplitude-frequency characteristics, phase noise of the spectrum of the input and output signal, weight, size and power characteristics of the AOM control system. These studies in the future make it possible to trace the influence of the characteristics of the AOM control system on the accuracy of modulation of the frequency of laser radiation and, as a consequence, on the accuracy characteristics of the QSF.

Author Keywords: cesium quantum frequency standard with optical pumping and detection

articleTitle: Accuracy of Determining the Objects Coordinates in TDoA Positioning Systems Taking Into Account the Attenuation of UWB Signals in the Range-Variant Radio Channel
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The accuracy of determining the objects coordinates in the time difference of arrival (TDoA) positioning system based on an algorithm for the exact analytical solution of hyperbolic equations is assessed. A ultra-wideband (UWB) signal in the form of the second derivative of a Gaussian pulse is used as a transmitter signal when simulating the assessment of positioning accuracy. The base stations (BSs) are supposed to use optimal receivers. Fluctuations in the arrival time of UWB pulses at base station (BS) receivers are determined by the attenuation of the signal as it propagates from the target transmitter to the BS receivers.
