During simulating that fluctuations in the arrival time determine the standard deviation of determining the coordinates of the object, that is, the accuracy of the positioning system. It has been established that the proposed algorithm for the exact analytical solution of hyperbolic equations ensures uniform accuracy in determining the coordinates of an object in the TDoA positioning system working area and a low root-means-square (RMS) value when determining the coordinates of an object.

articleTitle: Ab Initio Calculations of Band Structures of Bulk BaTiO3Based on Density Functional Theory with Hybrid Functional
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This article presents the results of modeling the band structure of barium titanate based on density functional theory using general gradient approximation (GGA), local density approximation involving orbital-dependent potential (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{LDA}+\mathrm{U}$</tex>), and the hybrid functional with exact exchange from Hartree-Fock (HF) method. The applicability criterion for the approximation used was the estimation of the band gap for cubic, tetragonal and orthorhombic phases of barium titanate and comparison of the obtained values with experimental data. It is shown that the hybrid three-parameter Becke-Lee-Yang-Parr functional provides the best agreement of calculating and experimental results for the band structure of BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. Thus, when using it, the obtained differences in the values of the band gap for the three phases under consideration do not exceed 13%, while using the Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhov functional for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{LDA}+\mathrm{U}$</tex> and GGA approximations gives a discrepancy with experimental data at 32% and 42%, respectively.

articleTitle: Assessing Polarization Stability in a Michelson Interferometer with Faraday Mirrors
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: We explore the polarization fading in a fiber-optic Michelson interferometer equipped with Faraday mirrors. Polarization fading can occur when the rotators within the mirrors experience faults. We propose a method for identifying the vulnerability of the interferometer to polarization fading in the case of a rotator malfunction. This approach only requires varying the state of polarization at the interferometer's input. Notably, it proves adequate to only vary the azimuth of linearly polarized light.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of DCO-OFDM, ACO-OFDM and ADO-OFDM Under the Influence of Optical Effects
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This article discusses methods of transmitting OFDM signals, such as DC biased optical OFDM (DCO-OFDM), asymmetrically clipped optical OFDM (ACO-OFDM) and asymmetrically clipped DC biased optical OFDM (ADO-OFDM), in a fiber-optic communication system with intensity modulation and direct detection (IMDD). A simulation model of data transmission over an optical channel has been developed in MATLAB to estimate the noise immunity in various cases. The optimal parameters minimising the bit error rate (BER) for DCO-OFDM and ADO-OFDM under relative intensity noise (RIN) and chromatic dispersion (CD) conditions have been determined. Based on the results, the effectiveness of the investigated methods of generating OFDM signals for systems with IMDD has been evaluated.

articleTitle: Photoluminescence of 1300 nm Range Strained InGaAs/InGaAlAs Superlattices
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The work presents the results on the creation and investigation of their optical properties of several heterostructures based on short period strained superlattices which are differed in the compositions of the waveguide layer and the average indium molar fraction. It is shown that heterostructure with superlattice based on In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.74</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.26</inf>As/In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.53</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.25</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.22</inf>As layers demonstrates the highest integral photoluminescence which is associated with the highest proportion of indium in the InGaAs layer and simultaneously with a high proportion of aluminum in the In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.53</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.25</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.22</inf>As layer which leads to an increase in the effective potential barrier for charge carriers in superlattice.

articleTitle: Measurement of External Impact by an Intermodal Fiber Interferometer with Spectral Interrogation and Fourier Transform of Output Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The approach to measuring external impact by measuring the phase difference of excited mode groups of an intermodal fiber interferometer has been experimentally investigated. The proposed approach is based on obtaining the phase spectrum of the spectral transfer function of an intermodal fiber interferometer. The results of measuring the external impact (the change in the length of the multimode fiber according to the triangular law) by the proposed approach are presented. It is shown that the method of measuring the phase difference of excited mode groups provides a linear response to external impact in a large dynamic range.

articleTitle: Potential of Brain-Computer Interfaces in Dementia
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This comprehensive review delves into the fundamental principles, technological advancements, and recent applications of Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs) in the field of dementia research. Dementia, a progressive neurodegenerative disorder, poses significant challenges to patients, caregivers, and healthcare professionals. With the integration of 6G network technology, BCIs offer a promising avenue for enhancing diagnosis, treatment, and the quality of life for individuals affected by dementia. The review explores the potential applications of BCIs in dementia research, including cognitive assessment, neurofeedback training, communication assistance, and therapeutic interventions. Furthermore, the challenges, limitations, and future directions of BCI development in dementia research with 6G network integration are discussed, highlighting the potential impact on clinical practice and the overall well-being of dementia patients.

articleTitle: Optical Anisotropy of GRIN Lenses: Modeling Based on the Integrated Photoelasticity
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The conditions of applicability of the quasi-isotropic approximation of geometrical optics (single-trajectory approximation) for the case of coaxial incidence are discussed. For this case, the reconstruction of residual stresses distributions (the inverse problem of transversal translucency) is carried out for a number of GRIN lenses. Using these data as input for calculations within the framework of the “direct” problem in coaxial incidence, the radial distributions of optical phase difference (birefringence) are determined for the case of longitudinal ray propagation in a GRIN rods.

articleTitle: A Two-Stage Attention Based Efficient Second-Order Minimization Network for Planar Object Tracking
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Planar object tracking, which detects the posture change of the 2D objects in a frame-by-frame manner, plays a critical role in various practical applications including visual simultaneous localization and mapping, visual servoing, and augmented reality. However, in real world, current methods suffer from ubiquitous challenges such as motion blur, texture degradation, illumination change, and partial occlusion. In this article, we propose a new tracking pipeline to handle the preceding challenges. The main novelty of our method lies in two new modules. Concretely, we first propose a Perspective Matrix Selection Module (PMSM) to rectify the search range error caused by large motion displacement. Second, we design an efficient attention mask module to highlight the target object while mitigating the disturbance caused by scene occlusion. The proposed method is evaluated on the challenging dataset POT. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods by a large margin in terms of accuracy and robustness over various tracking challenges, such as rotation, scale change, occlusion, motion blur, and perspective degradation.

articleTitle: Single-Snapshot Time-of-Arrival Estimation by OANM in a MU-MIMO System with Prior Information Aided
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: By orthonormal atomic norm minimization (OANM), we may utilize the property of atomic separation-freedom to perform low-complexity direction-of-arrival estimation although only a single-snapshot of the received signal is used. In other point of view, estimations in angular-domain are highly related to processing in time-domain. In this paper, we apply our proposed OANM method to perform time-of-arrival (ToA) estimations. Out of expectations, OANM, with the aiding of prior information, also works with the outcome of ideal accuracy. Specially noted that, when atomic separation is close enough for estimations, OANM results in lower measurement error - its performance approaches to that of another high-complex method.

articleTitle: Estimation of the Polarizability of C60O2 Molecular Groups in the Condensed Phase
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: A large-sized fullerene molecule contributes to the significant dipole moment of C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> molecular groups. The application of the «grain-interlayer» model for describing the dielectric spectrum of a material consisting of layers with different conductivity types made it possible to estimate a dipole moment of 3.1 D. A polarizability equal to 120 Å<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> was calculated using the Clausius-Mosotti model and 150 Å<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> using the Kirkwood model. By constructing dependences of the polarizability and dipole moment on the depth of the fullerene film crystallite saturation with oxygen, we could evaluate the correctness of the chosen depth values at the resulting dielectric permittivity values.

articleTitle: Optical Methods to Study the Composition of Human Tissue-Based Hydrogels for 3D Bioprinting and Regenerative Medicine
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This work used optical methods (Raman scattering spectroscopy and FTIR spectroscopy) to study the samples of collagen-containing hydrogels for 3D bioprinting at the different production process steps. Integrity of essential organic components has been shown in the hydrogels manufactured from Lioplast® freeze-dried human bone tissue.

articleTitle: Fast and Efficient Multistage Pedestrian Detection Method Using Computer Vision with Applications to 5G/6G Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper presents a fast an efficient pedestrian detection method using computer vision. The method is based on a multistage approach combining motion or change detectors with heuristics and small size convolutional neural networks (CNN). The method is faster than direct application of larger CNNs but produces comparable results. Possible application of the method in 5G/6G millimeter wave communication systems is discussed.

articleTitle: Application of Simple Detection Algorithm with Decision Feedback and Optimization of Observation Interval at Transmission Rates Above the Nyquist Barrier
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The article presents a description of an algorithm for detection of bandwidth-efficient signals with controlled intersymbol interference using the decision feedback method. The algorithm uses observation interval optimization, which allows minimizing the influence of subsequent signals when analyzing the received signal. Aspects of the practical application of this algorithm are considered. The article describes the implementation of the algorithm when using software-defined radio platforms NI USRP for transmitting and receiving over a wireless communication channel.

articleTitle: Estimating Ag+ Electrical Mobility Using Alkaline Ion Conductivity Data
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper presents a comparison that makes it possible to estimate the coefficients of electrical mobility of silver ions introduced from an external source from the electrical conductivity of alkali ions when they are equivalently replaced during the electrolysis process, which can be useful in calculating gradient structures in gradient optics and photonics.

articleTitle: Federated Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Spectrum Sharing and Power Allocation for Mobile Communication System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The escalating demand for heightened performance in global mobile communication systems necessitates novel methods to optimize spectrum and communication resource utilization. Dynamic spectrum access in cognitive radio systems has garnered significant attention, particularly employing deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for resource allocation. In this paper, a federated DRL based algorithm is proposed to deal with both the spectrum access and power allocation quandaries in mobile communication systems. In the proposed algorithm, we model secondary users as learning agents, enabling them to acquire spectrum access and power selection strategies through training with local training and federated model aggregation. By sharing pertinent information and aggregating local models, users enhance the efficiency of the training process. The proposed approach is expected to promote channel access, resource efficiency, and user privacy in the future communication system.

articleTitle: Hydrogel-Forming Microneedles for Extracting Analytes from Biological Fluids
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Microneedles can be used for transdermal delivery of drugs, biological markers, analyte extraction, etc. Swellable hydrogel microneedles are often used for these purposes, which is associated with their low production cost, ability to dissolve in the human body, and rather large volume of the transferred substance. An important feature of needles of this type is their porous structure, capable of containing a certain volume of liquid. In this work, arrays (up to 40) of microneedles were fabricated from a solution of gelatin and polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP). The height of the needles is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$900\ \mu\mathrm{m}$</tex>, and the diameter is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$200\ \mu\mathrm{m}$</tex>. The microneedle arrays differed in the percentage of the components of the composition, which made it possible to evaluate the effect of the PVP content on the mass of the extracted substance. It was found that with an increase in the proportion of PVP in the material, the mass of the extracted substance increases and reaches a value of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$47\ \mu\mathrm{g}$</tex> (for a sample with a PVP content of 66.7%).

articleTitle: Effect of Gold Nanoparticle Size on the Properties of Etched Silica Pillars
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method for the formation of efficient photoconverters which optical band gap decreases due to the introduction of impurities (gold nanoparticles) into the oxide. Gold nanoparticles can act both as noticeable levels in the band gap and as plasmonic particles. The use of 2D geometry in this case allows you to significantly increase the effective transformation surface. Photo-induced current transfer through nanocomposite structures consisting SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layers activated with gold nanoparticles (AuNP) are under investigation. AuNPs are situated on top of SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nano-pillars. Nano-pillar array with AuNPs is prepared by previously described two-step technique using plasma etching. Optical and electric characteristics of these structure are investigated.

articleTitle: 6D Pose Estimation of Aircraft Based on Multi-Model Data
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Automated safeguarding is becoming a trend for future airports. 6D position estimation of aircraft objects can be a prerequisite for safeguarding operational robots. 6D position estimation aims at predicting the location, size, and class of key features in 6D space, which further helps to plan driving routes and avoid collisions. In this paper, we propose a cross-modal 6D object detection network, which can obtain the high-precision 6D attitude of the aircraft objects and provide data support for the robot support operation. It is a multimodal fusion detection network that takes RGB images and LiDAR point clouds as inputs and predicts oriented 6D bounding boxes. Specifically, an RGB image-based position estimation network and a point cloud data-based position estimation network are designed respectively, and a multimodal data-based position estimation network is designed based on the characteristics of the two networks to further improve the accuracy of position estimation. To verify the effectiveness of the method, experiments are tested on the publicly available dataset, and the results show that the accuracy and operation speed of the proposed networks in this paper meet the engineering requirements.

articleTitle: Experimental Study and Analysis of the Thermopower in the Yl-xCaxBa2Cu3-xZnxOy System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The work is devoted to the study of the temperature dependences of the thermopower, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex>, in HTSC of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}_{-x}\text{YiC}\mathrm{a}_{X}{}_{\mathrm{a}2}\text{BC}_{\mathrm{U}3-X}\text{Zn}_{X}\mathrm{O}_{y}$</tex> system with different contents of impurities varied in the range 0.025 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leq x\leq 0.2$</tex>. All the experimental <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S(T)$</tex> dependences were satisfactorily described within the narrow-band model that allowed us to calculate the parameters of the energy spectrum and charge-carrier system in samples of different compositions. As a result, the concentration dependences of the model parameters were obtained, which were then analyzed to identufy the effect of the simultaneous calcium and zinc introduction into the lattice on the energy spectrum of the studied system. Physical reasons for the revealed peculiatrities of these dependences are discussed.

articleTitle: Antibacterial Activity of Ag, Au and Au/Ag Alloy Nanoparticles Embedded in Glass
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Surface contamination is the major public health burden, therefore, the development of non-toxic antimicrobial materials is in focus. In this work, we provide a comparative study of the antibacterial activity of glasses that contain gold-silver alloy nanoparticles of governed composition and gold and silver monometallic nanoparticles. We reveal that the antibacterial activity of the glass with nanoparticles against the gram-negative bacteria E. coli depends on the proportion of silver in the nanoparticles: the higher the silver proportion, the greater the bactericidal effect.

articleTitle: The Luminescent Properties of CsPbBr3 Precipitated in Polyurethane
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The work presents a method of CsPbBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> crystals precipitation directly in a solution of polyurethane and dimethylformamide. The time dependence of luminescence spectra was studied for both unpolymerized solutions and the resulting multilayer films. The resulting film demonstrated the presence of two luminescence bands with a maximum at about 463 and 519 nm.

articleTitle: Thermoelectric Generator and DC-DC Converter for Low-Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper deals with the research of the thermoelectric generator and a DC-DC converter for low-power applications. A comprehensive model of a thermoelectric generator and a boost DC-DC converter has been developed. The results of the simulation with parasitic resistances and capacitances showed that the efficiency of the converter in a CCM reached 74% and in a DCM -70% with conversion from 0.51 V to 2.4 V.

articleTitle: Electrically Tunable CRLH Leaky-Wave Antenna Based on Ferroelectric Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The design of the CRLH unit cell with via-free topology was presented in this work. Such a topology allows simple integration of tunable elements. During simulation, results of measurements of ferroelectric tunable capacitors were used. For a substrate, the experimental material based on fluoroplast-4D (F4Dr) reinforced with fiberglass was considered. Full-wave simulation shows that 10 units cells leaky-wave antenna demonstrate gain ~5 dB with electrical beam scanning in range ~50 degrees in frequency range 2.35- 2.45 GHz.

articleTitle: Degradation of Luminescent Properties and Changes in the Phase Composition of CsPbBr3/Cs4PbBr6 Prepared by Cold Injection Wet Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The paper presents the results of a study of the time dependences of the photoluminescence integral intensity of CsPbBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/Cs<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>PbBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> nanopowders synthesized by cold injection wet chemical method, as well as the results of phase and granulometric analysis immediately after synthesis and 30 days later. It was established that there is a relative increase in phase CsPbBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, accompanied by an increase in the average particle size.

articleTitle: The Way to Analyse MD Simulation Results of Cluster Ion Bombardment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Molecular Dynamics (MD) is a simulation method commonly employed in scientific research, specifically in the field of solid state physics. In particular, MD is a valuable tool for analysing rapid processes that take place on the surface, such as the stopping and fragmentation of accelerated cluster ions, sputtering of the target material and the formation of crater and rim. These phenomena necessitate the analysis of substantial amounts of data, encompassing the velocity, coordinates, and energies of each atom in the simulation. In this contribution, we propose scalable and automated methods to analyse size of impact crater, rim characteristics, surface deformation and the energy and directions of sputtered particles. To illustrate the efficacy of these methods, we present results obtained during MD simulation of (100) Si crystal surface bombardment with accelerated C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</inf> molecules.

articleTitle: The Effect of Temperature on the Pulsed Electrical Strength of Polypropylene and Polycarbonate Films
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The pulsed electrical strength of 2 µm thick polypropylene (PP) and 2.5 µm thick polycarbonate (PC) films was investigated under pulsed conditions. The most probable values of breakdown strengths for the thin films studied were obtained using the Weibull distribution. It is shown that within the temperature range of 293-363 K the breakdown strength of PP is practically independent of temperature and is about 500 MV/m, whereas for PC it decreases linearly from 700 MV/m to 500 MV/m.

articleTitle: Influence of Stimulated Near-IR Radiation on the Intensity of Terahertz Photoluminescence in GaAs/AlGaAs Quantum Wells
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: The parameters of a structure with tunnel-coupled GaAs/AlGaAs quantum wells designed to generate terahertz radiation during intersubband electron transitions under conditions of interband optical pumping are calculated and optimized. The dependences of the integral intensity of terahertz radiation on the pump level are experimentally obtained. The influence of interband stimulated radiation in the near infrared spectral range on the characteristics of radiation in the terahertz range is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Search for New Solutions to Improve the Efficiency of Solar Cells Using in Saint Petersburg and Hong Kong
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper presents a comparison of the capacity for photovoltaic (PV) development in St. Petersburg and Hong Kong, with a focus on identifying key factors that contribute to PV module degradation in these regions and proposing possible strategies to mitigate these issues. These two cities are located on the coast of the sea and them have a strong sea wind. This allows comparison of solar panel degradation. By evaluating the local climate conditions, our research suggests that St. Petersburg, situated near the Arctic Circle, has greater PV capacity during summer months due to its longer daylight hours and less cloud coverage compared to Hong Kong, which is located on the subtropics. Data gathered from the Pulkovo Observatory indicates an annual degradation rate of 2.3 % for frost-removed PV modules, compared to 8.19 % for PV modules operating year-round. Degradation at the level of 2.3 % is since in St. Petersburg (frosts and sleet occur in April and October). To reduce degradation in St. Petersburg, we propose the removal of solar panels during frost as a feasible solution. In Hong Kong, we recommend using thermoplastic polyolefin (TPO), instead of ethylene vinyl acetate (EVA), as a sealant for PV modules. TPO has demonstrated outstanding durability in damp heat tests, indicating it as a viable alternative. Our analysis shows an annual degradation rate of 0.3 % for TPO-based PV modules and 0.7 % for EVA-based PV modules.

articleTitle: Method of Determining the Coordinates of Airborne Objects Using a Passive Bistatic Radar System Based on Signals from a Secondary Radar System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: A method of controlling secondary radar systems using a remote control station has been investigated. The analysis of the transmitted and received signals at this station is performed to determine the location of aircraft. The dependence of the accuracy of determining coordinates by Time Sum of Arrival (TSoA) and Angle of Arrival (AoA) method on the error magnitude in determining the necessary coordinate-informative parameters (times of receiving transmitted and received signals, rotation period of interrogator) from secondary radar system signals was studied. The principle of operation of the system was described, sources of errors that affect the accuracy of control system operation were identified, and an acceptable level for these errors to achieve the required precision was established. The degree to which each type of error considered affects performance results was also determined. Recommendations for placing remote control stations to achieve maximum possible accuracy were proposed.

articleTitle: Formation of Transparent Contacts to p-NiO by DC Magnetron Sputtering ITO
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: This paper investigates the optical and electrical properties of ITO films for their application as a transparent contact electrode to NiO films. The films were fabricated by magnetron sputtering at various parameters of the discharge power and oxygen content in the working gas mixture. Structural analysis showed an increase in the crystallinity of the films during their subsequent annealing. The films demonstrate high conductivity and transparency with an absorption edge higher than that of NiO films. The results of the study show a high potential for using ITO films to create a transparent electrode to NiO layers.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Characterization of 5.2 um Quantum-Cascade Lasers Grown by Molecular-Beam Epitaxy
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: We present the results on the fabrication and time-resolved spectral characterization of 5.2 um range quantum-cascade laser. 40 stages of active region are based on strain-compensated In0.6Ga0.4As/In0.44Al0.56As heteropair. The mutli-mode lasing was demonstrated in the 5.09-5.21 um spectral range for lasers with four-cleaved facets. The estimated values of the threshold current density and voltage at 80 K were about 1.1 kA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 15 V, respectively. The maximal lasing temperature for lasers with four-cleaved facets was about 210 K.

articleTitle: Reflection-Assisted Non-Line-of-Sight Ultraviolet Communication Based on Drone Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of high path loss non line of sight (NLOS) ultraviolet communication (UVC) systems that rely solely on atmospheric scattering, we have established a channel model for NLOS UVC with not only scattering but also reflection considered via Monte-Carlo (MC) photon-tracing method. The effectiveness of the above theoretical model and the feasibility of its application are verified through outdoor drone testing experiments. The experimental results indicate that setting a reflector in a NLOS ultraviolet communication system can reduce both background noise and channel path loss. This work verifies the feasibility of using unmanned aerial vehicle platforms to achieve ground reflection assisted communication.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Ytterbium-Based Non-Alloyed Ohmic Contacts to n-GaN
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Fabrication of electric contacts is one of the most important stages in the electronic devices manufacturing process. Recently, considerable attention is paid to non-alloyed ohmic contact studies, although the more conventional approach usually involves contact formation by rapid thermal annealing of the sputtered metallization. In this work the contact resistance of alloyed (Ti/Al/Ni/Au and Ti/Al) and non-alloyed (Yb/Au) ohmic contacts to n-GaN epitaxial films is compared. Ti/Al/Ni/Au alloyed ohmic contacts have the lowest resistance. However, it is found that the contact resistance values for non-alloyed Yb/Au and alloyed Ti/Al contacts are similar. Thus, low-resistance non-alloyed Yb/Au-based ohmic contacts to n-GaN are demonstrated.

articleTitle: IQ Imbalance Quadrature Demodulation Correction Using Deduced Dimension Matrix
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Wideband RF chips can meet the demand of flexible bandwidth configuration and achieve high-rate transmission. However, these functions require greater breakthroughs in the research and development of chips. To achieve high bandwidth and high order modulation, it is necessary to minimize the impact of the mirrored signal caused by the I/Q imbalance in RF transceiver. In this paper, to achieve higher image rejection ratio, we improve the previous wideband I/Q imbalance model, optimizes the I/Q imbalance at the receiver, and bring in the phase and amplitude differences of the local oscillator signal of the transmitter and receiver respectively. At the receiver, the improved QDC blind correction method is used to eliminate the mirrored signal generated by I/Q imbalance. Through the analysis, we find matrix in I/Q blind correction algorithm is redundant. We can eliminate this redundancy by taking a simple method, which can reduce the complexity, enhance the operational stability, and ensure the implementation effect of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Spectral and Luminescent Properties of Borosilicate Glass with CsPbBr3 Nanocrystals
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Experimental results of the study of spectral and luminescent properties of borosilicate glass with CsPbBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> nanocrystals were demonstrated. Changes in the absorption spectra with temperature and time had a non-monotonic increasing character. The maxima of the luminescence spectra also had a long-wavelength shift from 519 to 538 nm, which opens up prospects for precise local adjustment of the emission wavelength.

articleTitle: Scenarios for Co-Existence of Digital TV and 5G Broadcast Services in UHF Band
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Photonics (EExPolytech)
abstract: Transition to Digital Television (DTV) provides opportunities to release upper part of DTV UHF band for new types of wireless services. 5G Broadcast and Multicast systems are possible options for using this spectrum for providing new types of services to mobile devices. LTE-based 5G terrestrial broadcast system and 5G New Radio Multicast Broadcast Services are already included in 3GPP specifications, but deployment of these systems needs coordination with existing DTV frequency band plans. This paper considers a number of scenarios for co-existence of DTV and 5G Broadcast services in UHF band. Analysis and comparison of scenarios shows that typical use of 5G Broadcast blocks within 8 MHz DTV channels is not quite efficient. Almost 100 % use of spectrum may be provided by DTV channel bonding, UHF band segmentation and use of 8 MHz 5G Broadcast bandwidth considered in 3GPP Release 17. For 700 MHz band a possible option is use of Supplemental Downlink (SDL) sub-band (738–758 MHz). All these approaches need considerable work on re-arrangement of DTV channels and UHF band planning. UHF band segmentation and use of SDL may provide considerable parts of UHF spectrum to 5G Broadcast and Multicast services with minimal interference to DTV channels. Use of spectrally efficient signals may provide new types of wireless services in UHF band in the future.
